harness: chapter/qa-p23-context.html — investigation only. Measurement semantics and stability thresholds IDENTICAL to P14/P15/P21 (lexicon present + non-empty signature + 3 consecutive identical 180ms samples, 30s hard cap). Added read-only diagnostics only.

protocol.overlappingRuns: none — one run() at a time, awaited
protocol.persistence: per chapter, immediately, to localStorage kw_p23_run1 / kw_p23_run2

partOne_twoSweeps.comparisonBasis: ordered-surface fingerprint AND finding fingerprint per chapter, not aggregate counts
partOne_twoSweeps.verdict: the two independent full sweeps are identical for all 259 chapters at fingerprint level. Sequential full-sweep context does NOT change measurement results.

details.firstDivergence: none observable — the ordered-surface fingerprint is identical in every measurement, so there is no first differing surface to report. The P21 state (407 occurrences, extra HCM "Nein" at speaking/311) has never been reproduced.
none observable — identical fingerprint every time

partTwo_anomalies.note: this is the decisive result: the three chapters that deviated in the P21 sweep reproduce their isolated golden values INSIDE a full sweep, twice. The P21 readings are not a property of sweep context.

configurations.result: identical on both renders (msToStable 1500 then 1797 — timing moved, result did not)

configurations.config: 6. isolated target after fresh page reload

partThree_ordering.verdict: no ordering dependency of any kind. Preceding chapter, following chapter, repeated rendering, cumulative state and fresh-reload isolation all produce byte-identical results.

partFour_state.lexiconEntries: 7802 in every chapter measured, in both sweeps and every mini-sweep — no growth, no drift
partFour_state.styleSheets: 5 per chapter (4 linked + inline), inlineStyleTags 2 — constant
partFour_state.iframes: 1 in the driver at all times (driver replaces, never accumulates)
partFour_state.differencesObserved: only host heap (15.4MB → 71.1MB across a sweep) and htmlChars varying by ±180 chars on repeated renders of the same chapter (a1-11: 115688 / 115677 / 115868). The htmlChars jitter is popup/aria scaffolding, not learner content: occurrence count, node count and both fingerprints are unchanged across those same renders.

partFive_resource.anomalyPositions: a1-11 at position 11 (after a1-10, 3861 nodes), a1-21 at 21 (after a1-20, 1543 nodes), b2-07 at 124 (after b2-06, 3122 nodes) — none follows an unusually heavy chapter
partFive_resource.verdict: heap grows monotonically across a sweep as expected, but results do not change with it. b2-07 at position 124 (heap ~38MB) measures identically to b2-07 rendered first in a 3-chapter mini-sweep. No causal link established; correlation not treated as cause.

sigChangedWhileSettling.note: in 518 chapter measurements the gate signature NEVER changed between first observation and settle — the page was already fully linkified when first sampled

secondReadingAfter900ms.verdict: the engine does NOT keep mutating after the driver records the chapter: a second full engine run 900ms later produced identical occurrence, finding and fingerprint values in all 518 measurements

partSix_timing.timingVariedResultDidNot: msToStable ranged 361–2399ms across measurements of the SAME chapters (a1-11: 364, 365, 366, 1196, 1500, 1797) with byte-identical results — the gate is not the variable that produced the P21 readings

partSeven_classification.A_deterministicSweepContextContamination: DISPROVEN — two full sweeps are fingerprint-identical and both reproduce the isolated golden values
partSeven_classification.B_orderingDependentStateContamination: DISPROVEN — six ordering configurations, all identical
partSeven_classification.C_timingStabilityGateProblem: NOT SUPPORTED as the cause of the P21 readings — sigChangedWhileSettling 0/518, second-reading changed 0/518, and large msToStable swings produced no result change. NOT fully excluded as a mechanism available under conditions not reproduced here.
partSeven_classification.D_resourceMemoryPressure: NOT SUPPORTED — heap varied 15–71MB with no result change
partSeven_classification.E_driverReentrancyLifecycle: NOT TESTED HERE, and the most plausible remaining candidate. The P21 sweep is the one run where a concurrent run() loop is known to have existed in this project (phase 15 produced a 966-finding double-count on b2-68 from exactly that, and phase 21 required a mid-run localStorage key change plus a page navigation). This phase deliberately used one awaited run() and reproduced golden values every time.
partSeven_classification.F_unresolved: the ORIGIN of the P21 readings themselves remains unresolved. They are now proven non-reproducible under clean single-run conditions; no mechanism has been positively demonstrated.

conclusion.p21SweepRowsForTheseThreeChapters: not reproducible — treat as measurement error local to that run, not as data
conclusion.correctPostFixCorpusState: 156,299 occurrences / 1,405 findings / 37 HCM / 71 clean — measured twice, identically, at fingerprint level
conclusion.p21BaselineStatus: its 1,406/38 total is 1 finding and 1 HCM too high; everything else in it is confirmed
conclusion.fiveCssFixes: confirmed again — HCM 110 → 37 across both sweeps, and the five corrected chapters are HCM-free in both

nextExperiment: Test hypothesis E directly: instrument the driver to detect re-entrancy (a run-in-progress flag plus a per-chapter render-token check that discards a result if a second render started), then deliberately provoke it by starting two overlapping run() calls and confirm it produces exactly the P21 signature — occurrence undercount with an extra popup-dependent finding. If it does, the P21 anomaly is explained and the driver needs a re-entrancy guard, not the engine.
